name: Jawed Karim
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded YouTube in February 2005 at age 25 with Chad Hurley and Steve Chen; uploaded the site's first video 'Me at the zoo' on April 23, 2005.
early_history_summary: Born October 28, 1979 in Merseburg, East Germany, to a Bangladeshi researcher father (later at 3M) and German biochemistry scientist mother. Family moved West Germany then to St. Paul, Minnesota (1992). Attended University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (CS), interned at SGI, left for early PayPal engineering, then co-founded YouTube while starting Stanford CS graduate studies.
family_context_summary: Born in East Germany to scientifically trained parents (father later a 3M researcher; mother a biochemistry scientist at University of Minnesota). Immigrated via West Germany to Minnesota in 1992 after experiences of racism.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were scientists/researchers, providing a STEM-oriented household but not an internet-startup pedigree.
primary_early_advantage_tags: PayPal Mafia network, UIUC CS, scientific parents, immigrant path, video platform wave
evidence_summary: Karim co-founded YouTube at 25 after PayPal engineering and UIUC CS training. Scientific immigrant family provided STEM orientation; PayPal peers Hurley and Chen supplied complementary product and design strength. YouTube sold to Google (2006) for ~$1.65B; Karim took a smaller equity stake while studying at Stanford but still received substantial Google stock. Landmark first-upload identity plus founding credit is unambiguous.
starting_point: Born Merseburg, East Germany, 1979 to scientist parents; relocated to Minnesota in 1992; CS path via UIUC and early PayPal.
current_position: YouTube co-founder and early investor (YVentures); known for Airbnb seed and other tech investments; largely private life with occasional public commentary via the 'Me at the zoo' description.

trajectory.event: Joined PayPal as an engineer; met future YouTube co-founders Chad Hurley and Steve Chen.
Co-founded YouTube in February; uploaded the platform's first video in April while studying at Stanford.
Google acquired YouTube for about $1.65 billion in stock; Karim held a smaller but still multimillion-dollar stake.
Launched Youniversity Ventures (YVentures) with Keith Rabois and Kevin Hartz.
Became one of Airbnb's earliest seed investors.

name: Blake Mycoskie
category: Consumer brand / social enterprise founder (TOMS, earlier EZ Laundry)
milestone_by_age_26: Founded EZ Laundry while at SMU as a sophomore (~1996-97), scaled it to ~$1M sales with 40+ employees across three universities, and sold his share to his partner in 1999 at about age 22-23; later founded Mycoskie Media sold to Clear Channel.
early_history_summary: Born August 26, 1976 in Arlington, Texas; father an orthopaedic surgeon, mother an author. Partial tennis scholarship to SMU; Achilles injury ended tennis. Dropped out to build EZ Laundry, then outdoor billboard firm Mycoskie Media (sold to Clear Channel), competed on The Amazing Race 2 (2002, third place), later founded TOMS Shoes in 2006 at age 29.
family_context_summary: Raised in Arlington, Texas; father an orthopaedic surgeon and mother an author—professional upper-middle-class household with resources for private school and tennis.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents not in consumer retail or entrepreneurship dynasties; support was general professional-class rather than industry-specific.
primary_early_advantage_tags: serial early businesses, tennis competitiveness, family professional resources, customer problem spotting
evidence_summary: Mycoskie's TOMS fame arrived at 29, but EZ Laundry and Mycoskie Media created material entrepreneurial proof by his early twenties with real revenue and exits. Professional Texas family and competitive tennis provided soft platform; successive small businesses built execution reps before the one-for-one TOMS model. Bain later bought half of TOMS (2014).
starting_point: Born Arlington, Texas, 1976 to an orthopaedic surgeon father and author mother; competitive tennis through high school and SMU.
current_position: TOMS founder (sold majority stake; brand continues); co-founder of Madefor wellness; author and speaker on social entrepreneurship.

trajectory.event: Launched EZ Laundry at SMU after Achilles injury ended competitive tennis.
Sold EZ Laundry stake after scaling to multi-campus ~$1M sales.
Finished third on The Amazing Race 2 with sister Paige; built public profile.
Founded TOMS Shoes with one-for-one giving model after a trip to Argentina.
Sold 50% of TOMS to Bain Capital while remaining Chief Shoe Giver.
Co-founded Madefor wellness subscription with Pat Dossett.

name: Yvon Chouinard
category: Outdoor equipment / apparel founder (Patagonia, Chouinard Equipment)
milestone_by_age_26: In 1957 at age 18-19 began forging hardened steel pitons and selling them from his car to support climbing; this craft business became Chouinard Equipment and later seeded Patagonia.
early_history_summary: Born November 9, 1938 in Lewiston, Maine, to a French-Canadian handyman/plumber father; family moved to Southern California in 1947. Discovered climbing via falconry as a teen, taught himself blacksmithing, and by late 1950s was a leading Yosemite climber funding the lifestyle by making superior gear.
family_context_summary: Working-class French-Canadian immigrant household; father a handyman/mechanic/plumber. Family moved from Maine to Burbank area when Yvon was about nine.
parent_family_domain_summary: No outdoor industry inheritance; mechanical aptitude from father may have aided metalworking, but climbing gear was self-taught.
primary_early_advantage_tags: self-taught blacksmithing, Yosemite climbing scene, dirtbag craft business, clean climbing innovation
evidence_summary: Chouinard built a livelihood and category-defining gear company from backyard forging by age 18-19, long before Patagonia apparel (1973). Yosemite peer network and obsessive climbing practice substituted for capital or pedigree. Later environmental ownership transfer of Patagonia (2022) cemented legendary status.
starting_point: Born Lewiston, Maine, 1938 to a French-Canadian tradesman family; relocated to Southern California as a child; climbing via falconry as a teen.
current_position: Patagonia founder who transferred company ownership to environmental trusts (2022); climber, environmentalist, and author (Let My People Go Surfing).

trajectory.event: Bought a used forge and began making/selling hardened steel pitons from his car.
Participated in first ascent of the North America Wall on El Capitan with Robbins, Frost, and Pratt.
Formalized Chouinard Equipment with Tom Frost; expanded redesign of climbing tools.
Founded Patagonia apparel brand as soft goods overtook hardware sales.
Founded 1% for the Planet with Patagonia as founding member.
Transferred Patagonia ownership so profits fund climate work via trust structure.

name: Phil Knight
category: Athletic footwear founder (Nike / Blue Ribbon Sports)
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Blue Ribbon Sports (later Nike) with Bill Bowerman by handshake on January 25, 1964 at age 25, securing Onitsuka Tiger distribution for the western U.S. after a Stanford MBA paper and Japan trip.
early_history_summary: Born February 24, 1938 in Portland to newspaper publisher William Knight and Lota Knight. Ran track at University of Oregon under Bowerman; BBA 1959; Army Reserve; Stanford GSB MBA 1962 with a paper on Japanese running shoes. Met Onitsuka in Kobe (1962), imported samples, partnered with Bowerman, sold shoes from a green Plymouth Valiant.
family_context_summary: Portland professional family; father was a lawyer turned newspaper publisher (Oregon Journal). Middle/upper-middle class Eastmoreland upbringing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father's media/legal career was not athletic footwear, though it signaled professional status; no shoe-industry dynasty.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Bowerman partnership, Oregon track, Stanford MBA, Japanese supply arbitrage, CPA day job safety
evidence_summary: Knight's Blue Ribbon Sports founding at 25 is a textbook ≤26 material milestone. Oregon track under Bowerman plus Stanford strategy paper created product insight; Bowerman provided design legitimacy. Built Nike into a global icon; net worth tens of billions; major philanthropist to UO, Stanford, OHSU.
starting_point: Born Portland, Oregon, 1938; father a lawyer-turned-publisher; ran track at University of Oregon under Bill Bowerman.
current_position: Nike co-founder and chairman emeritus; major philanthropist (UO, Stanford Knight-Hennessy, OHSU Knight Cancer); Forbes net worth tens of billions; owner of Laika animation studio.

trajectory.event: Completed Stanford MBA; traveled to Japan and secured Onitsuka Tiger distribution rights.
Co-founded Blue Ribbon Sports with Bill Bowerman (Jan 25 handshake partnership).
Renamed company Nike; Carolyn Davidson designed the Swoosh for $35.
Nike IPO; athletic footwear brand scaled nationally.
Signed Michael Jordan; Air Jordan line transformed sports marketing.
Stepped down as Nike CEO after decades leading the company.
Published memoir Shoe Dog; retired from Nike board.
